newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends slightly firmer, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends slightly firmer, seen stable.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar ended slightly firmer on Thursday after a day of narrow-range trading, reflecting the U.S. currency's weakness overseas, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.495 to the U.S. dollar against Wednesday's T$27.501. Turnover was US$217.5 million.
Dealers said there was some U.S. dollar buying by a foreign bank in early trade that dragged the rate to an intra-day low of T$27.500, but the trend later reversed.
"U.S. dollar selling soon emerged and pushed the Taiwan dollar higher. Buying and selling forces are quite equal," said one dealer.
The rate was expected to move narrowly around T$27.500 in the near term, dealers said.
